definitions.explanation: A cooking method where ingredients are deep-fried directly in oil without any flour, breadcrumbs, or batter. Used as a suru verb.

examples.japanese: {野菜|やさい}を{素揚|すあ}げにする。
examples.english: To deep-fry the vegetables without batter.

examples.japanese: {茄子|なす}の{素揚|すあ}げはカレーによく{合|あ}う。
examples.english: Deep-fried eggplant without batter goes well with curry.

examples.japanese: {素揚|すあ}げにすると{素材|そざい}の{味|あじ}がそのまま{楽|たの}しめる。
examples.english: Deep-frying without batter lets you enjoy the natural flavor of the ingredients.

notes:
USAGE:
A cooking term commonly found in recipes. The {素|す} prefix means "plain" or "without additions," contrasting with {天|てん}ぷら (tempura, battered and fried) or {唐揚|からあ}げ (coated with starch or flour). Commonly used for vegetables like {茄子|なす} (eggplant), {蓮根|れんこん} (lotus root), and {南瓜|かぼちゃ} (pumpkin).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {素揚|すあ}げにする (to deep-fry without coating)
- {素揚|すあ}げした{野菜|やさい} (vegetables fried without batter)
- {素揚|すあ}げにして{塩|しお}で{食|た}べる (to deep-fry plain and eat with salt)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {天|てん}ぷら: tempura — battered and deep-fried
- {唐揚|からあ}げ: deep-fried with starch coating — typically for chicken
